hero.title: Experiences that shape the whole child
hero.subtitle: At Trium, students learn through making, performing, creating, and moving — building the confidence and character to thrive beyond the classroom.

experiences.title: Trium Innovators - Coding, Robotics & AI
experiences.intro: A hands-on tech track where students design programmes, build robots, and explore how artificial intelligence actually works.
experiences.description: Through experimentation, debugging, and iteration, they move from curious users of technology to confident creators of it.

experiences.title: Arts- Music and Dance
experiences.intro: At Trium, music, dance and arts sit on the timetable every week — not as an extra, but as a subject every student rehearses, performs, and creates in.
experiences.description: Through composition, choreography, and performance, children build discipline and expression that carry into everything else they do.

experiences.title: Visual Arts
experiences.intro: Visual arts sit alongside maths and language on the Trium timetable — a scheduled, assessed subject where children paint, sculpt, and design every week.
experiences.description: Through drawing, colour, and craft, students learn to observe closely, take creative risks, and communicate ideas words alone can't carry.

experiences.title: Sports
experiences.intro: Physical education at Trium runs daily, not weekly — sport is treated as essential to how children learn to lead, compete, and recover, not a break from the classroom.
experiences.description: Through games, fitness, and team sport, students build resilience, fair play, and the habit of pushing themselves further.

realWorldEducation.heading: The TRIUM “Real World Education” model
realWorldEducation.description: The TRIUM “Real World Education” focuses on utilization of the theoretical learning into practical application. Students will spend 5 days a month as “Bagless days” where they will work on special projects designed to take their learning into the real-world. In this, they will be guided by special mentors and teachers.

projects.title: The Kitchen Garden Investigators
projects.problem: Where does our food come from, and can we grow some ourselves?
projects.description: Students design and grow a kitchen garden, tracking how seeds become food. They observe what plants need to thrive, care for crops daily, and harvest ingredients for a class meal — connecting science observations to what lands on their own plate.
projects.focusDescription: Daily care and observation of the garden, watching how plants respond to sun, water, and soil.
realWorldConnections: Talking to a local nursery owner

projects.title: Map My Neighbourhood
projects.problem: How does our own neighbourhood work, and who keeps it running?
projects.description: Students survey their neighbourhood, mapping homes, shops, parks, and public services, then interview a local representative to understand how community resources and local government decisions shape the place they live.
projects.focusDescription: Students interview a ward councillor to learn how local services and decisions are made.

projects.title: The Weather Station Project
projects.problem: Can we predict tomorrow's weather better than the app?
projects.description: Students build a simple weather station, recording temperature, humidity, and wind daily, then compare their readings against official forecasts to understand how weather and climate patterns actually form.
projects.focusDescription: Students record temperature, humidity, and wind every day and log the results.

projects.title: Constitution in Our Colony
projects.problem: How do the rights in our Constitution show up in everyday life?
projects.description: Students investigate how constitutional rights and local self-government actually function in their own colony — from a Resident Welfare Association meeting to a visit to a local court — connecting textbook civics to lived experience.
projects.focusDescription: Students interview a lawyer or civic official to see rights and law in practice.

cta.heading: A fuller journey for every learner
cta.body: Give your child space to discover what they can do, make, perform, and become.
